title: Greater Breast Support Is Associated With Reduced Oxygen Consumption and Greater Running Economy During a Treadmill Running Task
publisher: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
claims: Fifteen female recreational runners aged 18 to 30, running more than 12 miles per week and with self-reported bra sizes from B to DD cup, completed 10-minute treadmill trials in low-support and high-support sports bras.
Relative oxygen consumption was 30.9 ± 7.1 ml/kg/min in the low-support condition and 28.7 ± 6.7 ml/kg/min in the high-support condition (p < 0.001).
Running economy was 88.6 ± 29.1 m/L O2 in the low-support condition and 95.2 ± 31.1 m/L O2 in the high-support condition (p < 0.001).
No changes were observed in cadence (p = 0.149), step length (p = 0.300) or ground contact time (p = 0.151).
The change in running economy correlated strongly with breast size (r = 0.807, p < 0.001).
It is reported that up to 72% of females experience breast pain during exercise-related activities, citing earlier surveys and studies.
Females with a D-cup breast size can experience vertical breast displacements as high as 20 cm when running without breast support, citing earlier studies.

A previous study with 10 participants (Risius et al., 2017) reported no significant changes in heart rate, oxygen consumption, running economy, minute ventilation or breathing frequency with greater breast support.
The authors concluded that greater breast support was associated with improved comfort and improved running performance, but the study is small and used two specific sports bra models.
